title: Cognitive behavioural therapy for tinnitus (Cochrane Review)
authors: Fuller T, Cabrera A, et al.
control: Waitlist, audiological care, TRT, other active controls
followUp: Mostly none beyond end of treatment
primaryOutcome: Tinnitus impact on quality of life (THI/TFI/TQ)

results.summary: CBT vs no treatment: SMD −0.56 (95% CI −0.83 to −0.30; ≈10.9 THI points lower; 10 studies, 537 participants; low certainty). CBT vs audiological care: THI −5.65 points (95% CI −9.79 to −1.50; 3 studies, 444 participants; moderate certainty). CBT vs TRT: −15.79 points (95% CI −27.91 to −3.67; ONE study of 42 participants; low certainty). Essentially no reported harms.
results.detail: Also reduced depression (SMD −0.34) and anxiety (SMD −0.45, very low certainty). Only weak, if any, effects on perceived loudness.

coi: Cochrane-standard declarations; independent of any manufacturer.
limitations: Mostly low-certainty evidence; almost no 6–12-month follow-up data.

title: UNITI-RCT: single versus combined treatments for chronic tinnitus
authors: Schoisswohl S, Langguth B, et al.
control: Head-to-head: CBT, hearing aids, structured counseling, sound therapy — alone vs in combination
primaryOutcome: Between-group difference in THI change, baseline to week 12

results.summary: Within-group THI change: −11.7 (single treatments) vs −14.9 (combinations); the between-group difference of ≈3.2 points was statistically significant (p=0.034) but below the ~7-point clinical-meaningfulness threshold. Paper verbatim: CBT and hearing aids alone had large effect sizes 'which could not be further increased by combination treatment.'
results.detail: The largest trial ever to compare tinnitus treatments head-to-head. Statistically significant, clinically marginal difference between strategies — the substantive finding is which single treatments performed best.

title: Internet-based audiologist-guided CBT for tinnitus: US randomized controlled trial

results.summary: Post-treatment TFI 36.6 vs 46.3 (Cohen d = 0.46). Clinically significant improvement in 57% vs 15% — by the paper's own reliable-change criterion, not the standard 13-point TFI threshold.
results.detail: Control was weekly monitoring (no active comparator). 1-year follow-up paper reported maintained efficacy (PMID 36353148).

title: TENT-A1: bimodal sound + tongue stimulation for tinnitus
authors: Conlon B, Lim HH, et al.
design: Randomized double-blinded comparison of three stimulation parameter sets
control: None — all three arms were active bimodal treatment
primaryOutcome: Within-arm THI and TFI change at end of treatment

results.summary: Pre-specified primary result: within-arm THI improvement, effect sizes d = −0.87 to −0.92 across the three arms (≈14 THI points pooled), p<0.001 — but the arms did not differ from each other, and no arm was a sham.
results.detail: The widely quoted '86.2% improved at 12 weeks / 80.1% sustained at 12 months' figures come from manufacturer materials, count ANY improvement among compliant completers (not clinically meaningful responders), and could not be verified in the paper itself. Because every arm received active treatment, the trial cannot separate device effect from placebo/natural course.

limitations: No sham or no-treatment arm; identical results across arms; headline percentages are company-derived.

title: TENT-A3 pivotal trial: sound-only vs bimodal stimulation (within-subject)
design: Multi-site single-arm within-subject: 6 weeks sound-only, then 6 weeks bimodal
primaryOutcome: Responder rate (≥7-point THI improvement) during the bimodal stage vs the point estimate from the sound-only stage

results.summary: The primary endpoint was NOT achieved in the full cohort: responder rate during the bimodal stage was 43.3% vs 63.3% during the preceding sound-only stage. Important: this is a sequential design — everyone got sound first, bimodal second, and the bimodal stage was measured from an already-improved baseline — so it is NOT evidence that sound beats bimodal, but neither does it show bimodal superiority. In the pre-specified moderate-or-worse subgroup (THI≥38 at stage start): bimodal 58.6% vs sound-only 43.2%, p=0.022.
results.detail: 96.8% of device-related adverse events were mild; no serious device-related AEs. This is the trial behind the FDA De Novo authorization — which rested on the severe-subgroup result.

coi: Funded by Neuromod; co-author H.H. Lim has a financial interest in the manufacturer.
limitations: Single-arm sequential design (no parallel control); full-cohort primary endpoint missed; benefit confined to the more severe subgroup.

title: Real-world Lenire outcomes: US clinic chart review
authors: Kasper D, May T, Crossland G, Lim HH.
n: 140 fitted (66 of 104 'bothered' patients analyzed at 12 weeks)

results.summary: Among the 66 bothered-tinnitus patients (THI≥38) with 12-week data, 81.8% (95% CI 70.9–89.3) achieved ≥7-point THI improvement; mean −23.8 points. Non-bothered patients showed essentially no change.
results.detail: Uncontrolled real-world data with substantial follow-up attrition (66/104) and counseling co-intervention; consistent with trials but cannot separate treatment from placebo/natural course.

coi: Senior author Hubert Lim is Neuromod's CSO; Neuromod funded chart-review support.
limitations: Retrospective, uncontrolled, manufacturer-linked, 37% attrition in the analyzed group.

title: Reversing synchronized brain circuits using targeted auditory-somatosensory stimulation (bisensory device RCT)
design: Double-blind randomized crossover (6-week active vs 6-week auditory-only control)
duration: 6 weeks per block, 30 min/day at home
primaryOutcome: CO-PRIMARY: TFI change AND tinnitus loudness level (psychoacoustic loudness matching, dB SL). THI was secondary.

results.summary: TFI after active treatment: −12.0 points (ITT, p<.001), −13.2 per-protocol (n=56) — within-participant changes at week 6; the control block did not produce clinically significant decreases. Loudness matching (co-primary): −5.8 dB SL ITT (p=.08) / −7.2 dB PP (p=.03) at week 6, deepening to −10.9 ITT (p=.001) / −14.1 PP (p<.001) by week 12 of the second active phase.
results.detail: ≥13-point TFI responders: 65% per-protocol / 53% ITT after active treatment vs 25%/20% after control. All change figures are within-participant during the bisensory blocks, not active-minus-control differences. Somatic tinnitus only. NIH-funded (RF1-MH114244).

coi: NIH-funded; Shore and Martel are Auricle Inc cofounders with equity/patent interests (disclosed).
limitations: Single-center; per-protocol n=56; somatic tinnitus subtype only; COVID disruptions.

title: Auditory-somatosensory bimodal stimulation desynchronizes brain circuitry (first human pilot)

results.summary: Reduced tinnitus loudness and TFI vs auditory-only; established the timing-dependent plasticity approach in humans.

title: TRTT: Tinnitus Retraining Therapy vs standard of care
authors: Scherer RW, Formby C, et al.
design: Multicenter placebo-controlled RCT (6 US military hospitals)
control: TRT vs partial TRT (placebo sound generators) vs standard of care

results.summary: TRT was not superior to standard of care — all three arms improved substantially (within-group TQ effect sizes −1.32, −1.16, −1.01) with few between-group differences. 77.5% (86/111 with data) achieved ≥7-point TQ reduction at 18 months.
results.detail: Follow-up analyses attribute most benefit to the counseling component, not the sound generators.

title: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy for tinnitus: meta-analysis
journal: Indian Journal of Otolaryngology and Head & Neck Surgery

results.summary: Pooled THI reduction −17.67 points (95% CI −23.50 to −11.84) vs untreated control.

title: Mindfulness-based cognitive therapy for chronic tinnitus: RCT
control: Intensity-matched relaxation training (active control — a tougher bar than waitlist)
primaryOutcome: Tinnitus Questionnaire (co-primary with CORE-NR), between-group adjusted difference

results.summary: MBCT beat active relaxation training by 6.3 TQ points post-treatment (95% CI 1.3–11.4, p=0.016, ES 0.49) and by 7.2 points at 6-month follow-up (95% CI 2.1–12.3, p=0.006, ES 0.56).
results.detail: Loudness ratings improved in both arms (non-specific). The reliable-change responder difference (59% vs 44%) was not statistically significant.

limitations: Specialist psychology setting; responder-rate difference NS.

title: CBT for insomnia in tinnitus-related insomnia: RCT
control: Sleep support group; audiology-based care (both active)
primaryOutcome: Insomnia Severity Index + sleep-diary measures (tinnitus distress was SECONDARY)

results.summary: More than 80% of CBT-I participants reported clinically meaningful insomnia improvement, vs 47% with audiology-based care and 20% in the sleep support group; tinnitus distress (secondary) also improved.
results.detail: Effects sustained at 6 months. (Finer-grained ISI point-differences circulate but sit behind the paywall and could not be verified against the full text — the responder figures above are from the abstract.)

title: Sound therapy (amplification devices and sound generators) for tinnitus (Cochrane Review)

results.summary: Crucially: NO usable data existed for any of the three main comparisons (sound therapy vs waitlist, vs placebo, or vs education alone). The 8 trials only compared device types — hearing aids vs sound generators vs combination devices — with insufficient evidence of any difference (low/very-low certainty).
results.detail: This is absence of evidence, not 'tested and found no better': trials answering the sound-therapy-vs-placebo question simply have not produced usable data. Sound remains widely used, low-risk, and valued by many patients.

limitations: The central question (vs placebo/no treatment) has never been answered with usable trial data.

title: Cochlear implantation and tinnitus: systematic review and meta-analysis
design: Meta-analysis of mostly prospective cohort studies

results.summary: Pooled within-group improvements after implantation: THI −14.0, TQ −15.9, tinnitus VAS −3.1. Note: the pooled VAS mixes annoyance, loudness, life-effect and awareness bands — it is NOT a pure loudness scale. The percept-level ranges come from Ramakers et al. (Laryngoscope 2015): tinnitus decreases in 25–72% and is completely suppressed in 8–45% of implanted patients — while 0–25% experience worsening.
results.detail: Also reported: ~9.2% new-onset tinnitus after implantation (Assouly, cited therein). All pooled changes are pre/post within-group in non-randomized cohorts.

limitations: Observational data; implant candidates only; VAS is a mixed tinnitus scale.

title: rTMS for tinnitus: meta-analysis of 16 RCTs

results.summary: Active rTMS beat sham post-treatment (THI MD −11.5) and at 1 month (−11.0). At 6 months the two big meta-analyses DISAGREE: this 2025 analysis found no significant effect (MD −4.26, 95% CI −10.28 to 1.76), while the 2020 meta-analysis (29 RCTs, N=1,228; PMID 33228598) found a small significant one (−6.53, 95% CI −11.41 to −1.66).
results.detail: Either way, even the significant estimates sit at or below the ~7-point THI clinical-meaningfulness threshold — the durability and magnitude problems are unresolved, not settled in either direction.

limitations: High protocol heterogeneity; 6-month durability disputed between meta-analyses.

title: Transcranial electrical stimulation for tinnitus: meta-analysis

results.summary: Small-to-moderate effects; significant loudness reduction only with lateral-temporal-area stimulation; prefrontal stimulation mainly helped comorbid depression/anxiety. Verdict: possible adjunct, not a standalone treatment.

title: Vagus nerve stimulation paired with tones: randomized double-blind pilot

results.summary: At 6 weeks, 50% of paired-VNS participants had clinically meaningful THI improvement vs 28% of controls; benefit concentrated in tonal, non-blast-induced tinnitus.
results.detail: The sponsor (MicroTransponder) later pivoted its paired-VNS platform to stroke rehabilitation (Vivistim, FDA PMA 2021); no tinnitus development since.

title: Systematic evaluation of the T30 neurostimulator (acoustic CR): double-blind randomized placebo-controlled trial
authors: Hall DA, Pierzycki RH, Thomas H, Greenberg D, Sereda M, Hoare DJ.
design: Double-blind randomized placebo-controlled trial with open-label extension (NCT01541969)

results.summary: No benefit over placebo on the primary outcome (p=0.85).
results.detail: The definitive independent test of acoustic coordinated reset. An earlier industry-co-authored commentary (Front Psychol 2017) had called the RESET2 program 'non-conclusive'.

title: Bimodal stimulation using vibration on the skin (Neosensory Duo)
authors: Perrotta MV, Kohler I, Eagleman DM.
design: Controlled study, tones + wrist vibration vs tones-only

results.summary: TFI change −17.9 (SD 18.2) with the wristband vs −7.5 (SD 15.4) with tones only (between-group p=.04). No sham vibration — participants knew whether they wore the wristband.
results.detail: The larger −21.8 figure the company quotes applies only to the baseline-TFI≥50 subgroup (n=18).

coi: All authors are Neosensory employees or its founder/CEO.

title: OTO-313 (intratympanic gacyclidine) Phase 2: negative trial
primaryOutcome: TFI responder rate (≥13-point reduction at weeks 4 and 8)

results.summary: FAILED: responders 26% (OTO-313) vs 36% (placebo), p=0.385 — placebo numerically better. Otonomy discontinued the program and subsequently dissolved.
results.detail: One of the cleanest demonstrations of the ~30–40% placebo response that plagues tinnitus drug trials.

title: Keyzilen (AM-101) TACTT2 & TACTT3 Phase 3 failures (registry records)
journal: ClinicalTrials.gov posted results (no peer-reviewed Phase 3 publication exists)
design: Randomized placebo-controlled Phase 3 trials (intratympanic esketamine gel)

results.summary: FAILED. TACTT2 posted results: loudness change 0.80 vs 0.63 placebo (p=0.32); TFI 10.4 vs 9.6 (p=0.63) — both endpoints failed. TACTT3 (NCT02040194) also missed its primary endpoint; results never posted or published. Sponsor exited otology (now Altamira Therapeutics).
results.detail: Failed on both a loudness construct and a distress construct. That no Phase 3 results were ever peer-review published is itself informative.

title: Pharmacotherapy for subjective tinnitus: network meta-analysis of 60 RCTs
design: Systematic review + network meta-analysis (>30 drug interventions)

results.summary: No approved drug exists; 78% of included studies had methodological concerns; evidence quality low to very low. Tentative signals (antioxidants, GABA agonists) are hypothesis-generating only and conflict with Cochrane.

title: Ginkgo biloba for tinnitus (Cochrane Review)

results.summary: Ginkgo 'may have little to no effect' on tinnitus; the evidence is very uncertain.

title: Zinc supplementation for tinnitus (Cochrane Review)

results.summary: No evidence that oral zinc improves tinnitus symptoms in adults.

title: Betahistine for tinnitus (Cochrane Review)

results.summary: 'Absence of evidence' of any effect on subjective idiopathic tinnitus vs placebo; well tolerated.

title: Notched music vs ordinary music: independent RCT

results.summary: No significant THI difference between tailor-made notched music and ordinary music (N=104).
results.detail: The Münster trials reported modest effects mainly on perceived loudness in tonal tinnitus.

title: Kalmeda app (mobile CBT-based therapy): RCT behind Germany's DiGA listing

results.summary: Significant TQ reduction vs control, Cohen d = 1.1 (p<0.001). Kalmeda is permanently listed in the German DiGA registry (#350, permanent since Dec 2021; prescribable, reimbursed) on this basis.
results.detail: Control was 3-month DELAYED treatment (waitlist-type), which inflates effect sizes vs sham-controlled designs — the d=1.1 is not comparable head-to-head with sham-controlled trials. A 9-month extension RCT was published in JMIR 2025.

title: Smartphone tinnitus app: double-blind sham-controlled RCT (Japan)

results.summary: At week 16: THI −16.8 (active) vs +3.6 (sham — the sham arm slightly worsened, which flatters the difference); between-group −20.4 points (95% CI −28.2 to −12.6); meaningful improvement 70% vs 27%.
results.detail: Per the authors, the first DOUBLE-BLIND sham-app-controlled RCT of a tinnitus digital therapeutic (earlier app RCTs were single-blind). Registration jRCTs032230359.

coi: Sponsored by Kyorin Pharmaceutical; several authors received sponsor fees.

title: Oto app RCT vs waitlist (Flinders University)

results.summary: Between-group TFI difference at 6 months: 16 points (p=.002, 95% CI 6–25); the app group's within-group drop was 9 points. Clinically meaningful (≥13-point) improvement: 32% vs 12% at 6 months, 21% vs 5% at 9 months (d=0.62; 9-month persistence d=0.54).
results.detail: Completer-only analysis with 32% dropout in the app arm vs 9% control; the PhD was co-funded by Oto Health and a co-author is Oto Health's CSO. The larger DEFINE non-inferiority trial (N=198, vs therapist care) concluded Dec 2024 but remains unpublished.

limitations: Unblinded, waitlist control, completer-only analysis, differential dropout.

title: Supervised physical therapy added to treatment for somatic tinnitus

results.summary: Adding a supervised physical therapy program improved somatic tinnitus severity. Older data: 2 years after TMJ-disorder treatment, 43% vs 12% (control) had decreased tinnitus.
results.detail: Roughly 68–80% of tinnitus patients can modulate their tinnitus with jaw/head/neck maneuvers — the percept itself changes with the body.

limitations: No large multicenter RCT yet; subtype definitions vary.

title: STOPMD-3: SPI-1005 (ebselen) Phase 3 in Meniere's disease — company-reported results

results.summary: Sponsor reports co-primary endpoints met; in the OPEN-LABEL extension, patient-reported tinnitus, vertigo and aural fullness improved ≥30% from baseline (p<0.001). Peer-reviewed publication not yet located — treat as company-reported.
results.detail: FDA Breakthrough Therapy designation granted December 1, 2025 — for HEARING LOSS in Meniere's disease, not for tinnitus. PubMed check (Sept 2026): still no peer-reviewed STOPMD-3 publication.

limitations: Unblinded tinnitus data; Meniere's population, not primary tinnitus.

title: QUIET-1: AUT00063 (Kv3 modulator) Phase 2a — terminated for futility

results.summary: Terminated early for futility; TFI change ~1.6 points despite therapeutic-range drug exposure.

title: Tinnitus — current developments (state-of-the-field overview)
authors: Mazurek B, Steinmetzger K, Boecking B, Hesse G, Brueggemann P.

results.summary: CBT 'remains the gold standard.' Neuromodulation's clinical effectiveness judged 'relatively low'; for bimodal tongue stimulation, significant effects only in moderate-severe tinnitus and 'proof of clinical relevance is still lacking.'

title: TENT-A2: different bimodal neuromodulation settings in a large randomized trial
authors: Conlon B, Hamilton C, Meade E, …, Lim HH.
design: Randomized comparison of stimulation settings (no sham arm)
control: None — all arms active; settings changed mid-treatment

results.summary: Paper's own numbers: THI −18.5 points at end of treatment (arms 1–2 average; arm-level range −14.2 to −21.2), −20.2 at 12-month follow-up; TFI −15.3 / −17.3; Cohen's d −0.7 to −1.4.
results.detail: The manufacturer's oft-quoted '20.3 points' corresponds to the 12-month follow-up THI (20.2 in the paper). As in TENT-A1, no sham: within-arm changes cannot be separated from placebo/natural course.

coi: Funded by Neuromod (manufacturer); Lim is CSO.

title: First US real-world Lenire cohort (Communications Medicine)

results.summary: 91.5% responder rate; mean THI improvement 27.8 points — open-label, uncontrolled real-world data.
results.detail: First of two US chart reviews (the second is Kasper 2026, Am J Audiol).

title: Prototype digital polytherapeutic for tinnitus: randomized single-blind controlled trial
design: Randomized single-blind controlled trial vs white-noise app

results.summary: TFI −17.8 points (polytherapeutic) vs −10.1 (white-noise app); clinically meaningful response 65% vs 43%.
results.detail: A prototype app trial with ~61 completers — the research ancestor of the TrueSilence commercial product, which has no product-level trials yet.

limitations: Completer analysis; single-blind; prototype ≠ shipped product.

title: Hyperbaric oxygen for idiopathic sudden hearing loss and tinnitus (Cochrane Review)

results.summary: Studies small and methodologically poor; 'the significance of any improvement in tinnitus could not be assessed'; no benefit for chronic (>6-month) tinnitus; routine use cannot be justified.

title: Acupuncture for tinnitus: systematic review and meta-analysis (18 RCTs)

results.summary: No significant effect on the primary VAS outcome vs control; evidence insufficient.

title: Acupuncture for tinnitus: umbrella review of systematic reviews

results.summary: Methodological quality of ALL systematic reviews rated generally low; positive results 'must be viewed with caution'.

title: Low-level laser therapy for tinnitus: meta-analysis with trial sequential analysis

results.summary: No significant benefit of LLLT on tinnitus; trial sequential analysis indicates further identical trials are unlikely to change the conclusion.

title: Non-invasive vagus nerve stimulation for tinnitus: systematic review

results.summary: Only small heterogeneous pilot studies exist; narrative synthesis only; evidence insufficient.
results.detail: A multicenter double-blind RCT of taVNS + notched music (Sun Yat-Sen, NCT05417711) is the first adequately sized test.

title: Tinnitus-matched sound during sleep (Levo): randomized trial
design: RCT: tinnitus-matched stimulus vs noise masker vs bedside sound generator

results.summary: The sound-match arm showed the greatest reduction in rated tinnitus intensity and TFI — small study, no long-term data.
results.detail: VA Portland site; sponsor-linked.

limitations: Small; no long-term follow-up; no independent replication.

title: EEG neurofeedback for tinnitus: randomized trial of opposite protocols
design: RCT: alpha/delta vs beta/theta neurofeedback vs control

results.summary: Both OPPOSITE neurofeedback protocols reduced intensity ratings equally — indicating a non-specific effect — with no THI benefit.
results.detail: The specificity claim behind EEG neurofeedback failed its test.

title: Venous sinus stenting for pulsatile tinnitus: pooled analysis of 28 studies

results.summary: In imaging-confirmed venous-stenosis pulsatile tinnitus: 91.7% improvement, 88.6% complete resolution after stenting.
results.detail: Observational only; patient selection is everything. A dedicated stent trial (BosSTENT, NCT07070089, N=90) is registered.
